artifact.name: 18-audit-coverage
artifact.scope: Audit worker artifacts in knowledgegraph/research/types against six campaign objectives and all required semantic partitions.
constraints: Worker artifacts, source, SPORE/, Ghidra state, and historical triage artifacts were not modified.
No new Ghidra, runtime, build, test, or game evidence was added.
Assessment distinguishes static evidence, inference, contradiction, and missing evidence.

determinism.ordering: JSON arrays and Markdown tables are ordered by stable IDs, partition IDs, or paths.

global_limits: No MSVC RTTI is present in SporeApp.exe; class and inheritance identity cannot be promoted from candidate proximity alone.
No positive original Cell, Space, Empire, Editor, UI, or persistence runtime trace is present.
Persisted-body absence is uncaptured evidence, not proof that decompilation is impossible.
The vtable scan reports 58,756 functions while the canonical triage/xref universe reports 58,757; scope drift is preserved.
Historical verification PASS or FINDINGS status is not original semantic truth.

partitions.scope: Canonical corpus identity, authority precedence, hashes, source manifest, conflicts, and follow-up leads.
partitions.coverage: Defines the denominator and preserves the major population/scope conflicts used by the audit.

partitions.scope: Simulator service composition, shared managers, Cell state, pool identity, accessors, and reconstruction spine.
partitions.coverage: Strong for selected service fields, direct global accessors, CellGame/pool anchors, and static lifecycle methods; incomplete for global writer/reset and exact runtime order.

partitions.scope: Gameplay/entity types, Cell state spine, fields, vtable candidates, lifecycle anchors, and reconstruction relevance.
partitions.coverage: Strong for Cell entity identity, pool/query, selected fields, and bounded lifecycle; creature/city/tribe and component ownership remain partial.

partitions.scope: Creature simulation, evolution, editable models, rigblocks, animation, ornaments, herd, and collectables.
partitions.coverage: Strong static layouts and named evolution/editor methods; partial concrete hierarchy, runtime semantics, and ownership.

partitions.scope: Stars, planets, orbital data, generation, terrain, climate, geography, managers, consumers, and serialization.
partitions.coverage: Strong for SDK fields, named consumers, orbit/terrain interfaces, and known conflicts; generation formulas, ownership, and runtime order remain open.

partitions.scope: Empire, player, diplomacy, trade, missions, star/planet records, inventory, and relationships.
partitions.coverage: Strong for major records, fields, registries, named transitions, and static method anchors; runtime ownership, generation, and complete serialization remain partial.

partitions.scope: Editor, input, UTFWin, message, layout, controller, rendering, and UI-object types.
partitions.coverage: Strong for cEditor/EditorModel/input/message/Window surfaces and static method families; incomplete full subclass inventory, command grammar, dispatch order, and runtime ownership.

partitions.scope: Message records, listeners, handlers, queues, UTFWin dispatch, mode events, animation events, deferred events, feedback, comms, space records, and commands.
partitions.coverage: Strong for separating nine event families and documenting layouts, producers, consumers, and static dispatch boundaries; queue ordering and several payloads remain partial.

partitions.scope: Resource databases, Property/PropertyList, serializer interfaces, saved-game headers, Cell persistence, and format gates.
partitions.coverage: Strong architecture and declared interfaces; missing exact PROP wire format, SPO framing, serializer bodies, round-trip, and runtime order.

partitions.scope: DBPF, RW4, GMDL, raster, world-object, Cell records, content graphs, handles, and terrain/audio/metadata content.
partitions.coverage: Strong for key identity, selected record layouts, nested content graphs, and bounded current decoders; partial for runtime load/placement, GMDL v9, unknown sections, audio, shaders, and terrain.

partitions.scope: Application/Simulator accessors, service slots, registries, pools, allocators, vtable families, and replaceable boundaries.
partitions.coverage: Strong for 66 SDK Get anchors, direct slots, registry layouts, main pool, and service boundaries; partial unnamed slot identities and initialization/teardown order.

partitions.scope: Candidate vtables, slot status, SDK associations, high-value records, families, consumers, inheritance candidates, and contradictions.
partitions.coverage: Strong for 33 high-value records and global candidate accounting; not a complete class or slot inventory.

partitions.scope: High-value field offsets, read/write consumers, shared layouts, current-source comparisons, contradictions, and semantic ceilings.
partitions.coverage: Strong for 15 high-value offset groups and 6 shared layout groups; partial full-field semantic recovery and ownership.

partitions.scope: Construction, initialization, registration, enter/update, reuse, exit, dispose, pools, managers, cleanup, and exception paths.
partitions.coverage: Strong static phase coverage and selected sequences; missing exact global order, destructor/refcount balance, several removal paths, and runtime validation.

partitions.scope: Class/interface family inventory, address-bearing trees, ctor/dtor records, factory candidates, and contradictions.
partitions.coverage: Large inventory with 1,250 nodes, but only 33 class-specific binary virtual-slot matches and 1,199 naming-only families; hierarchy and ownership remain weak.

partitions.scope: Gameplay importance, reuse, unknown-unlock leverage, reconstruction classification, interface anchors, and ordered priorities.
partitions.coverage: Strong as a research prioritization artifact; not implementation authorization, effort estimation, or runtime validation.

partitions.scope: Unowned wrapper forests, buffer/string/map candidates, unattributed vtable, record pair, exclusions, and next actions.
partitions.coverage: Strong as an explicit unresolved-corpus partition; it intentionally does not resolve the unknown type identities.

partition_verification.coverage_caveat: All required partitions exist, but presence is not equivalent to complete objective coverage; the semantic-domain set contains several partial partitions and the cross-cutting set contains major structural/runtime gaps.

objective_coverage.name: vtable archaeology
objective_coverage.scope_statement: Strong bounded archaeology of high-value vtable candidates, slots, SDK associations, prefix families, consumers, and contradictions; incomplete global class/slot ownership.

requirements.result: 3,081 candidate bases, 369 high-confidence, 871 medium-confidence, 1,841 low-confidence, 20 labels, 16,107 shared-slot clusters, and 300 pair clusters are recorded.

requirements.requirement: High-value vtable records and slot status
requirements.result: A 33-record high-value union includes per-record implemented/inherited/overridden/unknown slot status, raw method targets, SDK associations, and consumer counts.
cCellModeStrategy, PropertyList/DirectPropertyList, cEditor, cToolStrategy, IO/PFRecord, and selected app/UI/resource families are explicitly bounded.
Twelve prefix chains and two 21-slot UTFWin bases are recorded, but no RTTI exists, the bases are not uniquely canonical, and many trees are naming-only.
4,384 unknown-vtable implementation rows and thousands of unlabelled candidates remain; the artifact intentionally does not claim a complete map.

important_omissions: Global owner assignment for candidate bases
Complete method-address/slot-name map for all candidates
RTTI-backed or independently corroborated hierarchy
Resolution of mixed UTFWin/Sporepedia candidate contamination

objective_coverage.name: class/struct recovery
objective_coverage.scope_statement: Strong static type, structure, field, record, interface, and embedded-layout recovery across all semantic partitions; semantic identity and complete object ownership remain bounded.

requirements.result: The controlling inventory records 2,035 Ghidra structures, 25,546 fields, 1,895 SDK XML structures, and distinct historical populations.

The ten semantic-domain partitions enumerate core, entity, creature, world/planet, empire/space, editor/UI, event, persistence, asset, and manager types with selected sizes, fields, vtables, and contracts.
Most layouts explicitly separate SDK/community provenance, Ghidra export evidence, and current-source comparison.
Embedded vtable/interface layout is well covered, but structural embedding is not promoted to language-level inheritance without RTTI.
Large types retain opaque tails, SDK/export conflicts, and inferred semantics even where sizes and offsets are strong.

important_omissions: Row-level reconciliation of 1,895 SDK structures versus 2,035 Ghidra structures
Complete semantics for large tails such as cCellObjectData, cTribe, cVehicle, cGameDataUFO, and cCreatureBase
Reliable C++ inheritance identities for embedded interface families

objective_coverage.name: field archaeology
objective_coverage.scope_statement: Strong bounded recovery of high-value offsets, read/write accesses, shared layouts, and contradictions; not a complete semantic field graph for every structure.

requirements.result: Fifteen high-value offset groups cover CellGame, CellObjectData, query, Cell references, advection, Cell records, Space/Empire, input, EASTL, resources, inventory, UTFWin, and Space UI/editor.
Material field rows carry candidate structure, offset, consumer VA, access mode, behavior, evidence, and provenance.
Six shared layouts are called out, including cCellDataReference, ResourceKey, eastl::map, eastl::vector, inventory base, and UTFWin Window.
The artifacts correctly separate observed offsets from inferred or unknown meanings, but many high-impact fields remain inference or unknown.

requirements.requirement: Complete field graph for all 25,546 fields
requirements.result: The field report deliberately mines high-value groups; it does not classify every exported field semantically.

important_omissions: cCellObjectData +0x100 through +0x358 full AI, damage, projectile, health, and animation semantics
Query insertion, removal, partition, and iteration order
Field meanings for unresolved shared-state and editor/UI surfaces
Complete ownership/nullability/runtime-value relationships for exported fields

objective_coverage.name: lifecycle
objective_coverage.scope_statement: Lifecycle phases and selected static sequences are well represented across the dedicated and domain partitions; exact order, ownership balance, and runtime confirmation remain open.

requirements.result: Construction, initialize, register, enter/update, replace/reuse, exit, and dispose/destroy are explicitly separated.
Mode manager, Cell mode, CellGame, pools, CellGFX, CellUI, inventory/trading, communications, star regeneration, message manager, editor, species profile, and animation boundaries are covered.
The 28-byte pool, 920-byte element, 4,096 capacity, first-word free-list/self-index behavior, Cell GFX rebuild, and rollover pool are characterized.
Registration and release-before-replace patterns are recorded, but listener removal, service deregistration, and exact manager disposal are incomplete.

requirements.requirement: Complete global initialization and teardown order
requirements.result: No artifact establishes the complete application/mode/Simulator/Cell/UI/message/resource shutdown order.
No positive original runtime trace validates any lifecycle relation.

important_omissions: Global bootstrap and shutdown dependency graph
Exact ISimulatorStrategy registration/update order
Destructor/AddRef/Release balance for pooled, cached, message, and service objects
Listener/service deregistration and event completion/removal order

objective_coverage.name: class families
objective_coverage.scope_statement: The artifact set has substantial family inventory and several address-bearing prefix families, but the binary-vtable-backed portion is small and most families are naming-only.

requirements.result: The class-family artifact inventories 1,250 class/interface nodes, 278 ctor/dtor records, and 18 factory candidates.
Trees exist for App, DefaultRefCounted, IUnmanagedMessageListener, Resource, IO, Object, and other interface families, but many descendants have no class-specific binary vtable.
Only 33 nodes have class-specific binary virtual-slot matches; 1,199 families remain naming-only.
The corpus records SDK family associations, vtable-family associations, concrete anchors, and reconstruction relevance across the major domains.
No RTTI-backed hierarchy exists, and structural/prefix evidence cannot prove unique C++ ownership or runtime dispatch.

important_omissions: Conversion of naming-only families into address-bearing or runtime-anchored families
Unique owner mapping for the 3,081 candidates and 4,384 unknown-vtable implementations
Resolution of class-family projection conflicts and mixed namespace anchors

objective_coverage.name: reconstruction value
objective_coverage.scope_statement: Strong research prioritization and boundary assessment; suitable for planning a clean-room report, not for implementation authorization or runtime-complete claims.

requirements.result: Scores, bands, formulas, provenance IDs, uncertainty, domains, and high-leverage unlockers are recorded for the recovered type set.
The artifact distinguishes reproduce-layout, semantic-interface-only, and replaceable-infrastructure.
Identity, service, input, content, property, serializable, event, animation, player/empire, relationship/trade/mission, and UI anchors are explicit.
Cross-stage identity, service/lifecycle, Cell, gameplay owners, and editor/content boundaries are prioritized.

requirements.requirement: Implementation effort, runtime validation, and final behavior proof
requirements.result: The artifact explicitly does not rank implementation effort, authorize implementation, or provide runtime validation.

important_omissions: Effort and dependency estimates independent of static relevance
Runtime validation of gameplay importance and transition ordering
A final report claim that current source matches original behavior
Promotion from research anchor to implementation-ready contract

missing_requirements: Complete global class hierarchy and vtable ownership
Global lifecycle ordering and runtime validation
Exact persistence wire formats and round trips
Original runtime validation for gameplay and subsystem transitions
objective_summary.overall_assessment: The artifacts provide a strong static archaeology package and a reliable bounded reconstruction plan, but not a complete original-runtime or ABI-complete report.

important_omissions.omission: No positive original Cell, Space, Empire, Editor, UI, terrain, audio, or persistence trace is present.
important_omissions.effect: Static operation, transition order, field meaning, event routing, and lifecycle claims cannot be promoted to observed or verified behavior.

important_omissions.omission: SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI; most class-family nodes are naming-only and only 33 have class-specific binary slot matches.
important_omissions.effect: The artifacts support candidate families and structural interface embeddings, not a complete C++ hierarchy or unique runtime owner graph.

important_omissions.omission: The 3,081 candidate bases and 4,384 unknown-vtable implementation rows are not globally mapped to owners, complete slot vectors, constructors, and dispatch semantics.
important_omissions.effect: A large portion of virtual behavior remains structurally known but semantically unowned.

important_omissions.omission: The artifacts preserve conflicts for cCellModeStrategy projection overlap, 0x01490be8 Terrain/Sporepedia attribution, cGameData Write/teardown, cObjectPool names, cCellDataReference aliases, cGameData/Property layouts, and message-handler interpretation.
important_omissions.effect: The final report must preserve both claims and must not present a single resolved type or lifecycle story where the evidence conflicts.

important_omissions.omission: The cCellObjectData middle range, large object tails, query containers, unresolved shared-state slots, editor/UI fields, and many field ownership/nullability/runtime-value relationships are not fully recovered.
important_omissions.effect: The artifacts are suitable for bounded interfaces and selected compatibility anchors, not complete field-accurate reconstruction.

important_omissions.topic: global manager and service lifecycle order
important_omissions.omission: Writers, reset order, constructor ownership, complete ISimulatorStrategy registration, and global shutdown order for application, Simulator, Cell, message, editor, and resource services are not established.
important_omissions.effect: Service-level semantic interfaces can be proposed, but exact original initialization and teardown sequencing cannot be finalized.

important_omissions.omission: The 0x18-byte queue record, priority direction, tie ordering, handled-result semantics, listener removal, UTFWin bubbling, and animation dispatch route are unresolved.
important_omissions.effect: Event families are well separated, but exact cross-subsystem event order and ownership cannot be claimed.

important_omissions.topic: exact persistence formats and round trips
important_omissions.omission: PROP byte order, SPO container framing, serializer stream framing, class-object registry, Property layout conflict, and save/load call order remain unresolved.
important_omissions.effect: Architecture and declared interfaces are reportable, but exact compatibility or round-trip reconstruction is not ready.

important_omissions.omission: Planet generation, terrain/weather transitions, audio formats and channel ownership, GMDL v9, unknown RW4 sections, shader payload semantics, world-object placement, and resource package priority/cache behavior are open.
important_omissions.effect: Asset and content partitions are strong for bounded record contracts but do not support complete original content/runtime reconstruction.

important_omissions.omission: 1,199 of 1,250 class/interface family nodes are naming-only and lack class-specific binary vtable evidence.
important_omissions.effect: Family trees are useful as a coverage index and hypothesis map, not as a completed class map.

important_omissions.omission: Current OpenSpore source is deliberately non-authoritative for original behavior, and several current projections intentionally reduce original layouts, globals, input, UI, GFX, and persistence.
important_omissions.effect: Current source can support bounded correspondence and clean-room comparison, not original semantic completion.

important_omissions.omission: The artifacts preserve conflicting denominators for functions, structures, fields, SDK rows, triage categories, debt ownership, vtable clusters, and verification statuses.
important_omissions.effect: Any final report must declare the population and provenance for every count and must not merge incompatible populations.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Read-only decompile and disassemble the mixed 0x00b3d220-0x00b3d5a0 accessor region and all direct callers/writers of the 0x0167eac0 packed block; classify each return as pointer, scalar, view, factory, mode-derived, or unresolved.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: This is the shared-state and service-ownership prerequisite for nearly every domain partition.
required_output: Concrete manager/domain owner or explicit unresolved status
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Direct field access plus at least two independent consumers or a corroborated lifecycle chain.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Recover the 27-slot cCellModeStrategy candidate at 0x01485550 against the SDK IGameMode order, all constructor writes, vtable-reference consumers, and current source slot comments.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: Cell mode is a central lifecycle and input anchor, but the SDK interface, 27-slot candidate, and current IGameMode comments disagree.
required_output: Mode manager registration and enter/exit order
Separation of original ABI from clean-room interface
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Function-start targets, construction evidence, and at least one vtable consumer or mode-manager body.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Carve the unattributed 0x013f1a30 40-slot candidate by comparing its full slot vector against the 300 pair clusters, 12 prefix chains, SDK method anchors, construction sites, and caller set.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: This is the highest-value fully unowned vtable candidate and anchors the unknown-vtable implementation population.
required_output: Class/interface identity only if independently corroborated
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Stable slot-vector matching plus construction or caller evidence; RTTI or namespace proximity is insufficient.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Compare the competing 0x01490be8 Terrain/Sporepedia candidate and the mixed UTFWin/Sporepedia 40-slot candidates using exact slot vectors, SDK method anchors, construction writes, and all vtable-reference consumers.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: The artifacts preserve a material class-family contradiction that could contaminate Terrain, Sporepedia, and UTFWin reconstruction anchors.
required_output: Resolution or preservation of owner ambiguity
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Two independent structural anchors and a consistent owner explanation.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Recover the full serializer/property/persistence bodies and call sequence: PropertyList Read/Write, ClassSerializer Read/Write, cGamePersistenceManager access/load path, and representative callers.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: Persistence is a reconstruction anchor and current artifacts explicitly mark PROP/SPO wire formats and save/load order unresolved.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Bodies plus at least one original .prop or .spo oracle and a reproducible round trip.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Trace Cell per-frame and pool/Gfx lifecycle bodies 0x00e806b0, 0x00e5b2e0, 0x00e780a0, 0x00e74a20, and their GFX release/rebuild callees, including the unnamed arguments and continuation order.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: This is the highest-value bounded Cell lifecycle and gameplay state path, but its complete order and field semantics are unresolved.
required_output: Pool release/recreate and GFX ownership order
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Multiple consumer bodies and a positive original trace for runtime-order claims.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Perform a field-use closure for cCellObjectData +0x100..+0x358 and cCellQueryLinkedPool entry/header fields across combat, animation, query, rendering, and save/load consumers.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: This closes the largest field-semantic omission and determines which current projection fields are compatibility-critical.
required_output: Unknown field list with next query
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Cross-consumer agreement; one decompiler field name or current source name is insufficient.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Recover message queue registration and dispatch: AddListener/AddHandler/AddEntry, ProcessQueue/ProcessQueue2, MessageSend/MessagePost, RemoveListener/RemoveHandler/RemoveEntry, and UTFWin DoMessage/SendMsg.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: The event partition identifies nine families but does not establish queue order, priority, removal, or UTFWin propagation rules.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Bodies with corrected calling conventions and a representative dispatch trace.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Carve the unowned forwarding forest and opaque map family together: 0x00f47380, 0x00f473a0, 0x009276c0, 0x009289f0, 0x00e5c780, 0x00ba8420, and 0x00b21340.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: These high-fan-in candidates cross editor, simulator, terrain, UI, and game-global clusters and can unlock large unknown regions.
required_output: Retirement or demotion of source-purpose labels
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Exact register/stack contract and stable consumer evidence; fan-in alone is insufficient.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Recover the 00e39ab0 paired record ABI from its constructor and at least two independent consumers, including all 27-field/24-field offsets, sentinel handling, allocation, release, and serialization status.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: The record pair is a reusable event/tool ABI with only inferred field counts and a contested Simulator/Space owner.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Constructor and independent consumer agreement; retain INFERRED if absent from SDK export.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Trace star/planet generation and persistence bodies around 0x00bb4af0, 0x00bb4100, 0x00bb5b50, cPlanetRecord creation, cSolarSystem graphics, and terrain/weather load/unload.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: World/planet artifacts are rich in fields and names but explicitly lack generation formulas, weather transitions, and runtime order.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Bodies plus original-process or byte-level generation/serialization evidence.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Resolve the cCellDataReference alias and all 12 typed reference variants by comparing 0x00e82340 and 0x00e82420, construction/callers, and the exact reference graph used by Cell records.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: The reference record is a high-value identity/ownership anchor and the artifacts preserve a one-address boundary conflict.
required_output: Serialized ID versus runtime pointer distinction
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Construction, caller, and field-access agreement; retain both addresses if unresolved.

highest_value_follow_up_queries.query: Recover editor and animation message dispatch from cEditorAnimEvent Send/Post through IAppSystem and into AnimatedCreature/IAnimWorld, including event IDs and payload ownership.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.why: The event and editor partitions identify the route but not the final consumer, event-ID table, or renderer/pose ownership.
highest_value_follow_up_queries.do_not_promote_without: Typed body chain from producer to final animation/pose consumer.

supported_report_scope: Coverage and uncertainty matrix for all six objectives
Bounded vtable, structure, field, lifecycle, class-family, and reconstruction-value synthesis
Semantic partition index with cross-artifact contradictions
Research-only reconstruction anchors, priorities, and evidence gates
not_supported_report_scope: Complete C++ class hierarchy or complete vtable ownership
Complete field semantics for all structures
Exact global initialization and teardown order
Exact PROP or SPO wire compatibility and round-trip claims
Implementation authorization or source replacement decisions
blocking_conditions: No MSVC RTTI or complete owner map
Incomplete unknown-vtable and naming-only family populations
Missing exact persistence formats and round trips
report_support.recommended_report_position: Publish as a static archaeology and reconstruction-planning report with explicit evidence ceilings, preserved contradictions, and follow-up gates. Do not describe the current artifacts as runtime-complete, ABI-complete, or implementation-ready.
